item.title: Cape Ashizuri: Kochi's Wild Southern Point — Guide
item.description: Cape Ashizuri is the wild southern tip of Shikoku, a rugged headland where sheer cliffs drop into the vast Pacific and a graceful white lighthouse stands against endless blue horizons. Remote and elemental, it has an end-of-the-land grandeur, with a scenic walking path along the clifftops taking in rock formations, a natural arch and sweeping ocean views. Just behind the cape sits Kongofukuji, the 38th temple of the Shikoku 88-temple pilgrimage, a sub-tropical temple set among camphor trees that has drawn pilgrims for over a thousand years.

item.title: Katsurahama Beach and the Ryoma Statue — Guide
item.description: Katsurahama is one of Kochi’s most beloved beaches, a scenic crescent of sand backed by green pines and framed by rocky headlands where the Pacific rolls in. Long celebrated as a spot for moon-viewing, it is more a place for scenery than swimming — the waves and currents can be strong — and its great landmark is the towering bronze statue of Sakamoto Ryoma, the Kochi-born samurai visionary who helped bring about the Meiji Restoration and the birth of modern Japan.
